speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I see you are experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To understand the underlying cause, have you noticed any trouble swallowing or speaking, and do you experience drooping of your eyelids or double vision that improves when you close one eye?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The pattern of ptosis/double vision worsening with upward gaze and fluctuating weakness that improves with rest is classic for this autoimmune disorder; no further tests are required for this clinical picture.
